headline: Bond revolts, Gulf energy shock and heat-driven famines usher in an era of financial repression

events: French government collapses over budget; OAT-Bund spread blows out past 200bp and ECB activates TPI amid German court challenge
Drone and missile strikes on Gulf export terminals push Brent above $125 for six weeks; European gas prices triple
US imposes sweeping secondary tariffs on countries buying Chinese chips; China retaliates with rare-earth and battery-material export licensing
Record Atlantic hurricane season hits Gulf Coast refineries, compounding fuel shortages
AI capex boom continues but first large hyperscaler writedowns spook equity markets
Weak 30-year Treasury auction triggers a 'term-premium tantrum': 10-year yield hits 6.4% and the dollar falls sharply
Fed halts QT, launches 'market functioning' purchases and caps bill rates informally; US enters recession with unemployment rising to 6.8%
Contested US election produces weeks of protests and a narrow outcome rejected by a large minority
Egypt, Pakistan and Kenya default or enter restructuring; IMF resources stretched as US delays quota contributions
Chinese naval 'customs inspection' quarantine of Taiwan for 19 days disrupts chip supply before a face-saving de-escalation
G20 inflation peaks near 7% as energy, food, tariffs and weaker currencies stack up; central banks tolerate overshoot
Japan's BoJ loses control of JGB curve briefly; yen crashes to 210 before coordinated intervention and new yield-cap regime
UK and Italy impose bank holdings requirements for domestic sovereign debt - open financial repression spreads
Sahel-coastal West Africa war erupts as jihadist groups and junta coalitions clash over Gulf of Guinea ports
AI agents spread in back offices as firms cut costs; white-collar hiring freezes fuel graduate unemployment protests
South Asian heat dome and failed monsoon cut wheat and rice output; India bans grain exports and food prices spike globally
Famine conditions in parts of the Horn of Africa and Sudan; migration surges toward the Gulf and Europe
EU agrees on a joint 'Security and Energy Bond' of EUR 800bn, effectively mutualising part of defence and grid spending
Armed clashes on the India-Pakistan border after a major terror attack; two weeks of fighting before ceasefire
Solar and battery deployments accelerate in importing nations as energy security trumps cost; coal also rebounds in Asia
Uneasy stabilisation: inflation back near 4%, policy rates held below inflation, debt eroded slowly via negative real yields
Common Framework 2.0 restructures debts of nine countries with partial Chinese participation
US passes a deficit-reduction package with a VAT-style consumption levy amid mass protests
Firms using AI reach ~30%, concentrated in finance, logistics and public administration; productivity gains uneven
Warming hits 1.62C as record heat in Southern Europe forces daytime work bans in summer

winners: Energy-secure exporters with spare capacity (Norway, Canada, Brazil, Guyana)
Owners of real assets, defence firms and grid/battery manufacturers
India's and Vietnam's manufacturing hubs absorbing China-plus-one supply chains (despite food shocks)
Governments with domestic savers able to run financial repression (Japan, Italy) avoiding outright default
losers: Import-dependent low-income countries in Africa and South Asia hit by food, fuel and debt service
Young workers and renters in advanced economies facing high rents, frozen hiring and negative real savings returns
Bondholders and pensioners suffering negative real yields
Europe's energy-intensive industry, which shrank permanently
bullets: Advanced economies have quietly adopted financial repression: yield caps, mandatory domestic sovereign holdings and inflation running above target to erode debt.
The dollar remains dominant but weaker; gold and bilateral currency settlement gained share after the 2028 Treasury tantrum.
Trade has hardened into rival blocs with licensing regimes for chips, critical minerals and food; tariffs are a permanent fiscal revenue source.
Nine sovereign debt crises since 2027 have left much of Africa and South Asia under IMF programmes with austerity and widespread unrest.
Energy security drives the transition: renewables reach ~43% of electricity, but coal and LNG infrastructure also expanded.
Climate disasters - heat domes, failed monsoons, hurricanes - are now macroeconomic events, moving food prices and sovereign spreads.
AI diffusion continued at a moderate pace, mostly as a cost-cutting tool, worsening white-collar insecurity without a broad productivity boom.
Politics is polarised and populist; trust in institutions is near record lows and protests over cost of living are routine.
wildcard: A 19-day Chinese 'customs quarantine' of Taiwan in 2028 halted advanced chip exports before ending in a negotiated de-escalation.
image_description: In a sweltering Marseille at 6 a.m., a delivery worker loads a battery cargo bike before the midday heat ban, passing a bakery whose chalkboard lists bread prices in both euros and ration-points beneath a faded protest poster about pension cuts.
